newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed lower across the board on moderate interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Bond prices were marked down slightly today following a small hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a dealer said.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.52/98.57 compared with Tuesday's close of S$98.55/98.65, September 2001 at S$96.30/96.40 against S$96.40/96.50 and June 2003 at S$94.37/94.42 from S$94.52/94.62.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 2-7/8 2-3/4 percent versus Tuesday's 2-3/4 2-5/8 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.77/2.72 percent against Tuesday's yield of 2.65/2.60 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.72/2.67 percent from 2.68/2.63 percent.
